checks.detail: 2 subtasks, read from the schema reply
4 phases had the tools designed for them

breakdown.label: States that 301 is "Moved Permanently" and 308 is "Permanent Redirect", and that both indicate the target resource has been assigned a new permanent URI.
breakdown.detail: met, backed by verified evidence E1, E2. “Both HTTP 301 (Moved Permanently) and HTTP 308 (Permanent Redirect) indicate that a resource has been permanently relocated to a new URI.”

breakdown.label: States that a client following a 308 must not change the request method: a POST is repeated as a POST, with its body.
breakdown.detail: met, backed by verified evidence E4, E5. “If the original request was POST, the client must resend it as POST with the same body intact.”

breakdown.label: States that when following a 301 a user agent MAY change the request method from POST to GET (for historical reasons), which is the behaviour 308 exists to rule out.
breakdown.detail: met, backed by verified evidence E3, E4. “For historical reasons, user agents may change the request method from POST to GET when following a 301 redirect.”

breakdown.label: States that both 301 and 308 responses are heuristically cacheable, i.e. a cache may reuse them by default unless the method definition or explicit cache controls say otherwise.
breakdown.detail: met, backed by verified evidence E6, E7. “Both status codes are **heuristically cacheable** by default.”

breakdown.label: States that both codes are currently specified in RFC 9110 (HTTP Semantics), and that 308 was originally defined in RFC 7538, which RFC 9110 obsoletes.
breakdown.detail: partial, backed by verified evidence E8, E10. “RFC 9110 (HTTP Semantics), Section 15.4.9 (current standard)”

evidence.claim: 301 status code indicates that the target resource has been assigned a new permanent URI
evidence.quote: The 301 (Moved Permanently) status code indicates that the target resource has been assigned a new permanent URI and any future references to this resource ought to use one of the enclosed URIs.

evidence.claim: 308 status code indicates that the target resource has been assigned a new permanent URI
evidence.quote: The 308 (Permanent Redirect) status code indicates that the target resource has been assigned a new permanent URI and any future references to this resource ought to use one of the enclosed URIs.

evidence.claim: User agents may change the request method from POST to GET for a 301 redirect for historical reasons
evidence.quote: For historical reasons, a user agent MAY change the request method from POST to GET for the subsequent request.

evidence.claim: 308 does not allow changing the request method from POST to GET
evidence.quote: This status code is similar to 301 (Moved Permanently) ([RFC7231], Section 6.4.2), except that it does not allow changing the request method from POST to GET.

evidence.claim: Request method and body will not be modified by the client in a 308 redirected request
evidence.quote: The request method and the body will not be modified by the client in the redirected request.
A 301 response is heuristically cacheable; i.e., unless otherwise indicated by the method definition or explicit cache controls (see Section 4.2.2 of [CACHING]).
A 308 response is heuristically cacheable; i.e., unless otherwise indicated by the method definition or explicit cache controls (see Section 4.2.2 of [CACHING]).

Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) Request for Comments: 7538 ... The Hypertext Transfer Protocol Status Code 308 (Permanent Redirect) ... This document specifies the additional Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) status code 308 (Permanent Redirect).
